rules.law_name: Residential Rental Property Application Fee Limit
rules.effective_date_basis: This act shall take effect on the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment
rules.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes. The cap is adjusted annually based on positive CPI changes beginning the January 1 following enactment.
rules.key_value: $50, adjusted annually by CPI if CPI change is greater than zero

coverage.other_unresolvable: Does not apply to a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental application or similar fees for dwelling-purpose leases or subleases, except units in one-family or two-family dwellings and certain New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensees.

rules.exemptions: The fee cap does not apply to a dwelling unit located in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent, or to a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property.
rules.penalty: Violations are subject to a penalty of up to $500 for a first offense, up to $750 for a second offense, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense; the wrongfully charged amount is remitted to the applicant or prospective tenant from the collected penalty.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
